chains.title: TFAP2A loss-of-binding at the ref A allele reduces IRF6 enhancer activity

links.claim: TFAP2A binds the ref A allele more strongly than the alt G allele; TFAP2A is chosen because the element is an IRF6 oral-epithelial enhancer with an AP-2-like site and AP-2α is the craniofacial epithelial paralog implicated at this locus. No QBiC-SELEX data are supplied, so this is a literature/motif-based binding claim, not a direct QBiC measurement.
rs642961 lies in a distal IRF6 enhancer; the ref A allele preserves a functional AP-2-responsive enhancer, while alt G weakens it.
Weakened enhancer activity lowers IRF6 transcription.
The relevant cells are developing oral/craniofacial epithelial cells, including lip fusion epithelium.
Lower IRF6 dosage impairs epithelial adhesion/fusion and increases cleft lip risk.

predictions: ref A binds TFAP2A more strongly than alt G
A allele has higher enhancer activity in oral epithelial cells
alt G associates with lower IRF6 expression
alt G increases cleft lip risk
falsified_if: alt G binds TFAP2A more strongly than ref A
no allele-specific TFAP2A binding is detectable
A and G alleles show no differential enhancer activity in oral epithelial cells

chains.title: TFAP2C binds the alt G allele more strongly and creates a stronger IRF6 enhancer

links.claim: TFAP2C, a close AP-2 paralog with shared binding specificity, binds the alt G allele more strongly than ref A. No QBiC-SELEX data are supplied; this competing claim rests on shared AP-2 motif recognition and epithelial expression, not on direct allele-specific data.
The alt G allele creates or strengthens a TFAP2C-responsive IRF6 enhancer.
The stronger enhancer increases IRF6 transcription.
The effect occurs in oral/craniofacial epithelial cells.
Misexpressed or increased IRF6 perturbs epithelial fusion and increases cleft lip risk.

no TFAP2C occupancy is detectable over the element
G allele does not increase enhancer activity or IRF6 expression

chains.title: TP63 binds the ref A allele more strongly at a p63-dependent IRF6 enhancer

links.claim: TP63 binds the ref A allele more strongly than alt G. This is a competing explanation because TP63 is a key craniofacial epithelial TF in the IRF6 pathway; no QBiC-SELEX data are supplied, so this binding claim is not directly measured.
The variant lies in a TP63-responsive IRF6 enhancer; ref A preserves and alt G weakens it.
Weakened TP63-dependent enhancer activity lowers IRF6 transcription.
The relevant cells are oral/craniofacial keratinocytes or epithelial cells.
Lower IRF6 in these cells impairs lip fusion and increases cleft lip risk.
